clue.text: Make fast lap to secure Silver, perhaps

parts.note: to make something fast is to fix it in place, as with a peg
a lap of a journey or race is a leg

explanation.surface: An instruction to tie up a lap so that some silver is held safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' is a link here. Long John Silver, the one-legged pirate of Treasure Island, is the 'perhaps' example.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg-leg is also a person with a wooden limb, and the pirate Long John Silver is the classic instance.

clue.text: Sally holding up Eastern attire

indicators.note: in a down clue the witty remark sits below and supports the letter for Eastern

parts.note: a sally is a witty remark or quip

explanation.surface: Sally keeps an Eastern costume from falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name; it is a witty retort.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to fit out or furnish, and to attire is to dress or kit out.

clue.text: Philanderer sailed away with crew

indicators.note: away suggests letters gone off, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A womaniser left port on a ship with its crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' man is a flirt who enjoys female company and pursuing women.

clue.text: Priceless instrument soaring to top note

indicators.note: in a down clue the note is placed on top of the rest

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down clue soaring means rising, so the instrument's word is read upwards

parts.note: a sitar is an Indian stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A precious instrument climbs to reach its highest note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaring' turns SITAR into RATIS. 'Priceless' looks like invaluable; here it means costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means free of charge, for no payment.

clue.text: Properly directed to follow short-term satellite emission

indicators.note: the first phrase is placed after the second piece, following it

parts.note: a mo, short for moment, is a brief term of time
on beam means correctly aligned or on course

explanation.surface: A technical note about a brief signal sent out by a satellite on the right heading.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon is Earth's natural satellite, and a ray of light coming off it is a natural emission from it.

clue.text: Does it help one to get bearings from drawing room?

definitions.text: Does it help one to get bearings from drawing room?

parts.words: Does it help one to get bearings from drawing room?
parts.note: drawing here means attracting metal, as a magnet does; a navigator's direction-finding instrument works by that pull

explanation.surface: Whether something in the drawing room helps a person get oriented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing room' seems a parlour; read it as attracting, giving the magnet sense.
explanation.definitionFit: This navigational instrument has a magnetised needle that points north, giving direction.

clue.text: Pull rank to cancel order I've put out?

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed and set into a new order

explanation.surface: A superior cancelling an order, wondering if the speaker is put out.
explanation.definitionFit: To override is to set aside a decision by superior authority.

clue.text: Offers to wrap new ties

indicators.note: the word for offers wraps around the letter for new

parts.note: bids are offers, as at auction

explanation.surface: Gifts wrapped up as presents of new neckties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ties' looks like a noun, neckwear; it is the verb, fastens.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind is to fasten together with cord, as to tie does.

clue.text: Creature snarling at gorilla

indicators.note: snarled things are tangled, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal growling at a great ape.
explanation.definitionFit: This large reptile with powerful jaws is a kind of animal.

clue.text: Common prison dispute heard in courtyard

parts.note: quad, or quod, is a slang (common) word for jail

indicators.note: signals that the word for dispute is taken by how it is spoken, its silent W dropping

parts.note: a wrangle is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A quarrel in a prison yard can be heard from the courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' marks QUAD as slang for prison. 'heard' makes WRANGLE sound as RANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrangle is an enclosed square yard surrounded by buildings, as at a college.

clue.text: Flower would be nothing if cut

definitions.text: Flower would be nothing if cut

parts.words: Flower would be nothing if cut
parts.note: a flower is a thing that flows, a river; shorten this river's name by its last letter and it spells a word for zero

explanation.surface: A gardener's lament that a bloom loses all value once snipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, not a bloom. Remove the final E and NIL, nothing, is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of Egypt is a flower in the crossword sense of something that flows.

clue.text: Demand for parking in a small Parisian enclosure

indicators.note: the parking letter is placed inside the following words, which form an enclosure round it

parts.note: petite is the French for small
P is the standard map and road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A request for a parking space in a tiny enclosure in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosure' reinforces the container: A PETITE encloses P.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite is a desire or craving, a demand for food or for something wanted.

clue.text: Abdicate when son is put in to rule

indicators.note: the letter for son is placed inside the word for rule

parts.note: to reign is to rule as monarch
S is the usual abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A monarch steps down when the son takes over the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or office, to step down from it formally.

clue.text: Vehicle rejected by trading centre

indicators.note: rejected, turned back, so the word for trading centre is read backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market, a centre of trade

explanation.surface: A vehicle is turned away by a market.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle running on rails in the street.

clue.text: Pedigree dog's competition venue

parts.note: race means breed or stock, a line of descent
to dog someone is to track them

explanation.surface: Where a dog with a pedigree is entered in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like the animal; it is a verb, follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A racetrack is a course where races are held, a venue for contests of speed.

clue.text: Justify dropping of opening show

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for justify is dropped

parts.note: to vindicate is to justify or clear of blame

explanation.surface: A demand that someone justify abandoning the opening night of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or display, to show something.

clue.text: Give special attention to sect that's to collect tax

parts.note: a cult is a sect

indicators.note: the letters for that's gather the tax inside

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Focus on a sect whose aim is to gather taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's value added tax, a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To cultivate is to foster or nurture, to work at developing something.

clue.text: Friendly even when caught out

annotationWithheld.why: Friendly even when caught out (8): AMIABLE with C (caught) gives the answer, but 'Friendly' must be both the definition and the source of AMIABLE; no other word supplies it

clue.text: English comedian carrying on and making money

indicators.note: the comedian's word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a comic is a comedian
the setter's piece is meant as the two letters N and O

explanation.surface: An English comic keeps working and earns well.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'on' inside COMIC gives the wrong order; the letters must go in as N then O.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic venture is a profitable one, paying its way and so earning a return.

clue.text: Frolic in vessel on lake

indicators.note: in an across clue the vessel is put on, after, the lake letter

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
Noah's ark was a vessel

explanation.surface: Playing about in a boat out on the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or mischief, a romp.

clue.text: Ran off with notes to prepare for flight

parts.note: fled means ran away
G is a musical note
E is another musical note

explanation.surface: Someone bolted with banknotes to get ready for a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like money; it is two musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Young birds fledge when they grow feathers ready to fly.

clue.text: Still an intrusion likely to spoil the reception

definitions.text: an intrusion likely to spoil the reception

explanation.surface: A calm moment broken by an unwanted guest at a wedding reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reception' suggests a party; it is radio or TV reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmoving is one sense; the other is the crackling interference that spoils a radio or television signal.

clue.text: Host rising to accept thanks from all

indicators.note: the reversed word takes in the thanks
in a down clue rising means the word for host reads upwards

parts.note: a host is a lot, a great number
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A host stands to receive thanks from everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns LOT into TOL; 'Host' looks like a party-giver but means a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the whole amount, everything added together.

clue.text: Manifold, as 6 is of 3, for example

explanation.surface: An arithmetic lesson on many-fold numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold means having many parts; six is twice three, so it is a product of three by a whole number.

clue.text: Constitutional taken in terrible gales

indicators.note: the answer is held inside these clue words

explanation.surface: A walk undertaken in terrible gales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' looks like a walk; here it means lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Constitutional means permitted by the fundamental law, lawful.

clue.text: Packaged, we hear, and carried away

indicators.note: signals that the word for packaged is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: packaged means wrapped

explanation.surface: A parcel, we're told, was packed up and removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means enthralled, transported by delight or absorption.

clue.text: Garden ably cultivated on the whole

indicators.note: cultivated soil is worked over, so these letters are dug through and rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden tended well, taken overall.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means generally speaking, considering everything together.

clue.text: Cooks use them to finish off cakes on the outside

indicators.note: the word for cakes goes round the outside of the word for finish off

parts.note: to cake is to set hard, so cakes means sets
to finish off is to kill

explanation.surface: Kitchen tools used to complete cakes by decorating their outer edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cakes' looks like food but is a verb, sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan, a utensil found in every kitchen.

clue.text: Fairly flat and extremely lengthy

parts.note: a flat surface is an even one

indicators.note: takes only the extreme, first and last, letters of lengthy

explanation.surface: A description of something quite level and very long.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means justly, without favour, as fairly does.
